claim: Calcium-alginate can show a lag followed by rapid disintegration when Ca2+ crosslinks are lost
value_or_observation: Complete dissolution in a short interval after a lag; dextran release became pulsatile
conditions: Ca2+/Mg2+-free PBS, pH 7.4; alginate gel beads
source_title: Pulsed dextran release from calcium-alginate gel beads
transfer_warning: Drug-release bead geometry and PBS chemistry are not dishwashing conditions

claim: Ca-alginate swelling/degradation can be driven by ion exchange and Ca2+ release
value_or_observation: Ca-crosslinked beads: ~160% water uptake then dissolution; Ca2+ release was diffusion-controlled
source_title: Investigation of swelling/degradation behaviour of alginate beads crosslinked with Ca2+ and Ba2+ ions
transfer_warning: Bead composition/size and PBS ionic strength differ from proposed porous composite

claim: Alginate wet modulus is tunable via ionic-crosslinking process
conditions: SA-Ca(II) hydrogel; neutral solutions; ambient fabrication
source_title: A Shapable Alginate Hydrogel Resolving the Conflicts between Multifunctionality and Fabrication Simplicity
transfer_warning: Specific fabrication and formulation; use only as scale evidence until full methods are encoded

claim: Cellulose nanofibrils can reinforce Ca-alginate while preserving swelling
value_or_observation: 5 wt% MCNF increased compressive modulus 36%; 5 wt% CMCNF increased it 17%
source_title: The effects of morpholine pre-treated and carboxymethylated cellulose nanofibrils on the properties of alginate-based hydrogels
transfer_warning: Modified CNF chemistry may not satisfy final simplicity/safety constraints

claim: Porous alginate sponge structure is controllable by formulation and freeze processing
value_or_observation: Macroporous sponges reported with ~70–300 µm pores
conditions: Alginate gelled with bivalent cations, frozen, lyophilized
source_title: Novel alginate sponges for cell culture and transplantation
transfer_warning: Biomedical scaffold target; no timed failure requirement

claim: Pullulan provides a water-soluble strong film-forming sacrificial phase
value_or_observation: Pullulan film tensile strength 67 MPa and elongation 11%; dissolved faster than alginate or CMC films
conditions: 55% RH, 20 °C for mechanical values; solvent-cast films
source_title: Preparation and properties of pullulan–alginate–carboxymethylcellulose blend films
transfer_warning: Dry film tensile data cannot be used as wet sponge modulus; exact dissolution times must be extracted from full data

claim: Water strongly plasticizes pullulan and changes mechanical response
value_or_observation: Large decreases in tensile modulus/strength with increasing water content were reported
source_title: Molecular weight effects on solution rheology of pullulan and mechanical properties of its films
transfer_warning: Moisture-plasticized film behaviour is only mechanistic support, not a sponge lifetime model

claim: Calcium pectin can swell and dissolve as calcium crosslinks dissociate
value_or_observation: Marked swelling and eventual dissolution as free Ca2+ concentration decreases; reported Ca-binding stability constant ~8000 for the tested pectin gel
conditions: High-methoxyl tomato pectin gel, pH 6 binding study / aqueous salt swelling
source_title: Calcium binding and swelling behaviour of a high methoxyl pectin gel
transfer_warning: Pectin source/DE and calcium chemistry strongly affect transferability

claim: Crosslink ratio tunes wet pectin mechanics
value_or_observation: Dynamic modulus fell from 5.5e4 to 3.5e4 Pa between 30 and 60 °C for crosslink ratio 0.36
conditions: 2% pectin calcium gel; immersed in water
source_title: Swelling behaviour of calcium pectin hydrogels by thermomechanical analysis in water
transfer_warning: Temperature range exceeds ordinary dishwashing; single formulation

claim: Crosslink duration can create qualitatively different swelling/degradation timing
value_or_observation: 1-min crosslink: degradation starts ~30 min; 5-min crosslink: swelling to ~240 min, plateau ~240–360 min, degradation after ~360 min
conditions: 4% w/w low-viscosity alginate; 100 mM CaCl2; 1- or 5-min crosslink; 1-min distilled-water rinse
source_title: Swelling, degradation and calcium release study of calcium-alginate beads
transfer_warning: Bead geometry and wet conditions differ from porous cellulose-reinforced CleanCoin

claim: Preparation residence time changes calcium distribution and downstream physical properties
value_or_observation: Internal Ca2+ increased with residence time to a later plateau while surface Ca2+ saturated earlier; particle size, porosity, density, strength and swelling changed with IGRT
conditions: Low-viscosity alginate particles; ionotropic Ca crosslinking; residence-time study
source_title: The effect of ionotropic gelation residence time on alginate cross-linking and properties
transfer_warning: Particle/drying/drug-loading protocol differs from A01; use to justify preparation-history state, not direct parameter transfer

claim: Effective crosslink density maps quantitatively to modulus and network mesh size in an unswollen reference gel
value_or_observation: At 3.8% alginate: E=47.587 kPa, rho_x=6.4 mol/m3, xi=7.9 nm, lambda1=20.1 s
conditions: High-G alginate; 50 mM CaCl2 + 0.4 M NaCl; 3-day homogeneous crosslink; 25 C mechanics; no post-crosslink swelling/shrinkage
source_title: Structural Characterization of Calcium Alginate Matrices by Means of Mechanical and Release Tests
transfer_warning: High-G/long-crosslink reference; Flory relation is an unswollen reference law, not A01's swelling-state constitutive law

claim: Monovalent-ion exposure can strongly soften Ca-alginate
value_or_observation: After 15 h physiological NaCl exposure: compressive modulus -63%, equilibrium shear -84%, dynamic shear -90% vs controls
source_title: Compressive and shear properties of alginate gel: effects of sodium ions and alginate concentration
transfer_warning: 15-h endpoint is much slower than CleanCoin target and source formulation differs; use as weakening magnitude evidence

claim: External citrate can dynamically soften Ca-alginate on a tens-of-minutes timescale
value_or_observation: 500 mM sodium citrate reduced G-prime by about one order of magnitude; 500 mM EDTA drove G-prime near uncrosslinked level after ~35 min
conditions: 4% alginate (M:G 0.39:0.61); 20-min external crosslink with 200 mM CaCl2; 1-mm rheometer gap; chelator source substituted in situ
source_title: In situ rheological measurements of the external gelation of alginate
transfer_warning: Very high external chelator concentrations; dynamic mechanism benchmark only, not product dose or safety evidence

claim: Stable-gel plateau modulus follows an alginate-specific calcium-distance scaling
value_or_observation: Ge = k * epsilon^1.5 where epsilon is relative Ca2+ distance above the gel point; fibril diameter/network density increase with Ca2+
conditions: Alginate gels across alginate and Ca2+ concentrations; gel point determined by Winter-Chambon criterion
source_title: Scaling law and microstructure of alginate hydrogel
transfer_warning: Prefactor and gel-point Ca concentration are formulation-specific; total Ca inventory is not the same as the gelling variable

claim: Alginate swelling kinetics can follow a second-order law and depend strongly on calcium and G fraction
value_or_observation: Second-order swelling fits; rate generally decreased as calcium increased; low-G LF240D and intermediate-G HF120 series tabulated from 12.5–40 mM Ca
conditions: 5 mg/mL alginate; internal CaCO3/GDL gelation; tablets immersed in 50 mL double-distilled water
source_title: A quantitative analysis of alginate swelling
transfer_warning: 0.5% alginate and internal gelation differ strongly from A01; several conditions show syneresis/negative fitted constants and must not be reused as positive swelling rates

claim: Loss of network constraint during aqueous incubation can greatly enlarge alginate mesh size
value_or_observation: Initial mesh 4–20 nm; after 10 days aqueous culture medium incubation all formulations increased to ~30–250 nm; initial modulus ranged 3.91–18.4 kPa across selected formulations
conditions: 1–2% alginate beads crosslinked using 100–200 mM CaCl2; long aqueous incubation
source_title: Gel microstructure regulates proliferation and differentiation of MC3T3-E1 cells encapsulated in alginate beads
transfer_warning: 10-day biological-medium timescale is much slower than CleanCoin; useful as structural coupling evidence, not timer calibration
